name: Peter
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: A fisherman from Bethsaida, named first in every list of the Twelve.
story: A fisherman from Bethsaida whom Jesus named Cephas, or Peter; named first in every list of the Twelve, he denied Jesus three times and spoke for the apostles.

entries.title: From Bethsaida; a house at Capernaum
entries.text: Scripture says Philip “was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). In Capernaum Simon and Andrew had a house (Mark 1:21, 29), which Matthew calls “Peter’s house” (Matt 8:14).

entries.title: A fisherman with Andrew
entries.text: A fisherman, casting a net with his brother Andrew (Matt 4:18). James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were his “partners” (Luke 5:10).

entries.title: Andrew’s brother
entries.text: His brother was Andrew, who brought him to Jesus (John 1:40–42).

entries.title: The son of Jona
entries.text: His father is called Jona (John 1:42) and Jonas (John 21:15–17); Jesus calls him “Simon Bar-jona”, son of Jona (Matt 16:17).

entries.title: A married man
entries.text: He was married. Jesus healed “Simon’s wife’s mother” at his house (Mark 1:29–31), and Paul says Cephas took “a wife” with him on his travels (1 Cor 9:5). Scripture does not give her name or mention children.

entries.title: Choosing a twelfth apostle
entries.text: He stands up among about 120 believers and leads the choosing of one to take Judas’s place (Acts 1:15–26).

entries.title: Pentecost
entries.text: At Pentecost he speaks for the Eleven (“Peter, standing up with the eleven”), and about three thousand are baptized (Acts 2:14–41).

entries.title: The lame man at the temple gate
entries.text: With John he heals a lame man at the temple gate and speaks in Solomon’s porch (Acts 3:1–26).

entries.title: Arrested with John
entries.text: He and John are arrested and questioned by the council, who see that they are “unlearned and ignorant men” and that “they had been with Jesus” (Acts 4:1–22).

entries.title: Ananias and Sapphira; the council
entries.text: He confronts Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:1–11). People lay the sick in the streets so that “the shadow of Peter passing by” might fall on them (Acts 5:15). Before the council, “Peter and the other apostles” say, “We ought to obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29).

entries.title: Sent to Samaria
entries.text: He is sent with John to Samaria, where they lay hands on the new believers and Peter rebukes Simon the sorcerer (Acts 8:14–25).

entries.title: Lydda and Joppa
entries.text: At Lydda he heals Aeneas; at Joppa he raises Tabitha and stays with Simon a tanner (Acts 9:32–43).

entries.title: Cornelius at Caesarea
entries.text: After a vision at Joppa he goes to the Roman centurion Cornelius at Caesarea, and the Holy Ghost falls on Gentiles (Acts 10:1–48). He defends this in Jerusalem (Acts 11:1–18).

entries.title: Prison, and the angel
entries.text: Herod kills James and then imprisons Peter; an angel leads him out. He goes to the house of Mary the mother of John Mark, then “departed, and went into another place” (Acts 12:3–17).

entries.title: The council at Jerusalem
entries.text: At the council in Jerusalem he speaks for receiving the Gentiles (Acts 15:7–11). This is the last time Acts names him.

entries.title: Paul stays fifteen days; the pillars
entries.text: Paul went up to Jerusalem “to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days” (Gal 1:18). Later James, Cephas and John “seemed to be pillars” and gave Paul and Barnabas “the right hands of fellowship” (Gal 2:9).

entries.title: Withstood at Antioch
entries.text: At Antioch Paul “withstood him to the face” for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles (Gal 2:11–14).

entries.title: A wife on his travels; “I of Cephas”
entries.text: Paul says Cephas travelled with a wife (1 Cor 9:5), and some at Corinth said “I of Cephas” (1 Cor 1:12).

entries.title: “By Silvanus … at Babylon”
entries.text: 1 Peter is written “By Silvanus” and sends greetings from the church “at Babylon” and from “Marcus my son” (1 Pet 5:12–13).

entries.title: Clement of Rome, 1 Clement 5
entries.text: Peter “endured not one nor two but many labours, and thus having borne his testimony went to his appointed place of glory.” No place and no manner of death is given.
entries.when: about AD 95–96, at the close of Domitian’s persecution (Lightfoot, 1891)

entries.title: The Acts of Peter (apocryphal), chs. 35–37
entries.text: Leaving Rome, Peter meets the Lord and asks, “Lord, whither goest thou”; told “I go into Rome to be crucified”, he turns back. He asks to be crucified “with the head downward and not otherwise”.
entries.when: not later than AD 200 (M. R. James, 1924)

entries.text: Peter “appears to have preached in Pontus, Galatia, Bithynia, Cappadocia, and Asia” and “at last, having come to Rome, he was crucified head-downwards; for he had requested that he might suffer in this way.”

entries.title: Eusebius, Church History 2.25.5
entries.text: “It is, therefore, recorded that Paul was beheaded in Rome itself, and that Peter likewise was crucified under Nero.”

entries.title: Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men 1
entries.text: Peter was bishop of Antioch, reached Rome “in the second year of Claudius”, held “the sacerdotal chair there for twenty-five years until the last, that is the fourteenth, year of Nero”, and was “nailed to the cross with his head towards the ground”.

cols.label: Mark 1 · By the sea of Galilee

verses.text: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:
And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
¶ When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.
He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am?
And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.
And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ.
¶ And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cæsarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
¶ And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say, Elias; and others say, that one of the old prophets is risen again.
He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.
And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;
And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,
And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
Then answered Peter, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.
And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.
¶ And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
¶ And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
¶ Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.
But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.
And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.
And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
¶ And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilaean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
¶ Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilæan.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
¶ And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.
But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.
And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.
And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.
One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.

claim.text: Luke tells the call with a great catch of fish from Simon’s boat. Robertson’s harmony sets Luke 5:1–11 beside Matthew 4 and Mark 1 as one event (section 41).
His brother, who brought him to Jesus (John 1:40–42). They fished together and shared a house (Mark 1:16, 29).
A fishing partner (Luke 5:10). With Peter and John, one of the three Jesus took into Jairus’s house, up the mountain, and further into Gethsemane (Mark 5:37; 9:2; 14:33).
A fishing partner (Luke 5:10), sent with Peter to prepare the passover (Luke 22:8), and with him at the temple, before the council and in Samaria (Acts 3:1; 4:13; 8:14).
Paul says Cephas took “a wife” with him (1 Cor 9:5).
The centurion at Caesarea who sent for Peter (Acts 10:1–8, 24–48).
Paul stayed with him fifteen days in Jerusalem, and later opposed him at Antioch (Gal 1:18; 2:11).
On his visit to Peter, Paul saw no other apostle “save James the Lord’s brother” (Gal 1:19).

Freed from prison, Peter went to the house of Mary, “the mother of John, whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12). 1 Peter sends greetings from “Marcus my son” (1 Pet 5:13); our people data treats the two as one man.
Papias (early 2nd century), quoted by Eusebius, says Mark “having become the interpreter of Peter, wrote down accurately … whatsoever he remembered”.
1 Peter is written “By Silvanus, a faithful brother” (1 Pet 5:12). Our people data treats Silvanus as Paul’s companion Silas.

family.text: His brother was Andrew, who brought him to Jesus (John 1:40–42).
His father is called Jona (John 1:42) and Jonas (John 21:15–17); Jesus calls him “Simon Bar-jona”, son of Jona (Matt 16:17).

He was married. Jesus healed “Simon’s wife’s mother” at his house (Mark 1:29–31), and Paul says Cephas took “a wife” with him on his travels (1 Cor 9:5). Scripture does not give her name or mention children.
Clement of Alexandria (about AD 200), as quoted by Eusebius, says that Peter had children, and that “they say” Peter saw his own wife led out to die and called to her, “Remember the Lord.”

identifications.text: Jesus told Simon, “thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone” (John 1:42), and in Matthew, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church” (Matt 16:18). Paul uses both names for the same man in two neighbouring verses (Gal 2:8–9).
The KJV gives his father’s name as Jona or Jonas. Tischendorf’s Greek text in the site library reads ‘son of John’ at John 21:15, and our people data files the father under the name John.
The “Simeon” of Acts 15:14 is taken to be Peter because James is replying to Peter’s speech just before (Acts 15:7–11). Our people data files the verse under Peter.

scripture.text: Jesus tells Peter that when he is old “another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not”. John adds: “This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God” (John 21:18–19).

The writer of 2 Peter, who names himself “Simon Peter” (2 Pet 1:1), says “shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me” (2 Pet 1:14). Who wrote 2 Peter is discussed on the Letters pages.
Acts last names him at the council in Jerusalem (Acts 15:7) and never says how, where or when he died.

tradition.text: Peter “endured not one nor two but many labours, and thus having borne his testimony went to his appointed place of glory.” No place and no manner of death is given.
tradition.when: about AD 95–96, at the close of Domitian’s persecution (Lightfoot, 1891)

tradition.text: Writing to the Roman church on his way to death, Ignatius says, “I do not enjoin you, as Peter and Paul did.”
tradition.who: Ignatius of Antioch, To the Romans 4

tradition.text: Peter and Paul “taught together in like manner in Italy, and suffered martyrdom at the same time.”
tradition.who: Dionysius, bishop of Corinth, letter to the Romans, quoted by Eusebius (2.25.8)
tradition.when: about AD 170, writing to Soter, bishop of Rome (Eusebius 4.23.9)

tradition.text: Matthew wrote “while Peter and Paul were preaching at Rome, and laying the foundations of the Church”, and Mark was “the disciple and interpreter of Peter”.
Luke’s Acts leaves out “the passion of Peter” because Luke wrote only what he saw himself.
tradition.who: The Muratorian fragment, an anonymous list of New Testament books

tradition.text: “I can show the trophies of the apostles. For if you will go to the Vatican or to the Ostian way, you will find the trophies of those who laid the foundations of this church.”
tradition.who: Gaius (Caius) of Rome, against Proclus, quoted by Eusebius (2.25.7)
tradition.when: about AD 200 (under Zephyrinus, bishop of Rome)

tradition.text: At Rome, “Peter endures a passion like his Lord’s”; elsewhere, “Then is Peter girt by another, when he is made fast to the cross.”
tradition.who: Tertullian, Prescription against Heretics 36 and Scorpiace 15

tradition.text: Leaving Rome, Peter meets the Lord and asks, “Lord, whither goest thou”; told “I go into Rome to be crucified”, he turns back. He asks to be crucified “with the head downward and not otherwise”.
tradition.when: not later than AD 200 (M. R. James, 1924)

tradition.text: Peter “appears to have preached in Pontus, Galatia, Bithynia, Cappadocia, and Asia” and “at last, having come to Rome, he was crucified head-downwards; for he had requested that he might suffer in this way.”
tradition.who: Origen, Commentary on Genesis book 3, as reported by Eusebius (3.1.2)
tradition.when: first half of the 3rd century; Eusebius about AD 325

tradition.text: “It is, therefore, recorded that Paul was beheaded in Rome itself, and that Peter likewise was crucified under Nero.”

Peter was bishop of Antioch, reached Rome “in the second year of Claudius”, held “the sacerdotal chair there for twenty-five years until the last, that is the fourteenth, year of Nero”, and was “nailed to the cross with his head towards the ground”.

questions.question: When did Peter come to Rome, and how long was he there?

views.label: He and Paul founded the Roman church together

argument.text: Irenaeus speaks of the church “founded and organized at Rome by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul”, who then “committed into the hands of Linus the office of the episcopate”. Neither writer says how long Peter stayed.

views.label: He came to Rome at the end of his life
views.holders: Origen (first half of the 3rd century), as reported by Eusebius

argument.text: After preaching in Asia Minor, Peter “at last, having come to Rome, he was crucified”.

views.label: He came under Claudius and led the church for twenty-five years
views.holders: Eusebius (about 325) for the arrival under Claudius; Jerome (392) for the twenty-five years

argument.text: Eusebius has Peter led to Rome “during the reign of Claudius”; Jerome dates it to “the second year of Claudius” and counts twenty-five years to Nero’s fourteenth year.

questions.question: Was the man Paul opposed at Antioch the apostle Peter?

argument.text: The KJV reads “Peter” in Galatians 2:11 and 2:14. Tertullian writes that “Peter was rebuked because, after he had lived with the Gentiles, he proceeded to separate himself from their company”.

views.label: No, another Cephas, one of the Seventy
views.holders: Clement of Alexandria (about 200), Hypotyposes book 5, as reported by Eusebius

argument.text: Clement “says that Cephas was one of the seventy disciples, a man who bore the same name as the apostle Peter”. Tischendorf’s Greek text in the site library reads “Cephas” in Galatians 2:11 and 2:14, where the KJV reads “Peter”.

notSaid: Scripture never says that Peter went to Rome, or how, where or when he died.
Acts does not say where “another place” was when Peter left Jerusalem after his escape (Acts 12:17).
Paul’s greetings to the church at Rome (Romans 16:3–16) do not name Peter.
Scripture does not name Peter’s wife and does not mention children.
Scripture does not give Peter’s age at any point.

verses.42009018: ¶ And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
verses.42009019: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say, Elias; and others say, that one of the old prophets is risen again.
verses.42009020: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.
verses.42009021: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;
verses.42009028: ¶ And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
verses.42009029: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
verses.42009030: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
verses.42009031: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
verses.42009032: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
verses.42009033: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
verses.42009034: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
verses.42009035: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
verses.42009036: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
verses.42012041: ¶ Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?
verses.42018028: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.
verses.42022008: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.
verses.42022031: ¶ And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
verses.42022032: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
verses.42022033: And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.
verses.42022034: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
verses.42022054: ¶ Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
verses.42022055: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
verses.42022056: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
verses.42022057: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
verses.42022058: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
verses.42022059: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilæan.
verses.42022060: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
verses.42022061: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
verses.42022062: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
verses.42024012: Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.
verses.42024034: Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.
verses.43001040: One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
verses.43001041: He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.
verses.43001042: And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.
verses.43001044: Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
verses.43006008: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, saith unto him,
verses.43006066: ¶ From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.
verses.43006067: Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away?
verses.43006068: Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.
verses.43006069: And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.
verses.43013006: Then cometh he to Simon Peter: and Peter saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
verses.43013007: Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter.
verses.43013008: Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
verses.43013009: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.
verses.43013010: Jesus saith to him, He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
verses.43013024: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spake.
verses.43013036: ¶ Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
verses.43013037: Peter said unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thy sake.
verses.43013038: Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for my sake? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.
verses.43018010: Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
verses.43018011: Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?
verses.43018015: ¶ And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.
verses.43018016: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
verses.43018017: Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.
verses.43018018: And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.
verses.43018025: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.
verses.43018026: One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
verses.43018027: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.
verses.43020002: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.
verses.43020003: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.
verses.43020004: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
verses.43020005: And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.
verses.43020006: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,
verses.43020007: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.
verses.43020008: Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.
verses.43020009: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
verses.43020010: Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.
verses.43021001: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself.
verses.43021002: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
verses.43021003: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
verses.43021004: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
verses.43021005: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.
verses.43021006: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
verses.43021007: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher’s coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea.
verses.43021008: And the other disciples came in a little ship; (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits,) dragging the net with fishes.
verses.43021009: As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
verses.43021010: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.
verses.43021011: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
verses.43021012: Jesus saith unto them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
verses.43021015: ¶ So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
verses.43021016: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
verses.43021017: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
verses.43021018: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
verses.43021019: This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
verses.43021021: Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
verses.44001013: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
verses.44001015: ¶ And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, and said, (the number of names together were about an hundred and twenty,)
verses.44001016: Men and brethren, this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus.
verses.44001017: For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.
verses.44001018: Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.
verses.44001019: And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.
verses.44001020: For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.
verses.44001021: Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
verses.44001022: Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.
verses.44001023: And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
verses.44001024: And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,
verses.44001025: That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.
verses.44001026: And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
verses.44002014: ¶ But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:
verses.44002015: For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.
verses.44002016: But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel;
verses.44002017: And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:
verses.44002018: And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy:
verses.44002019: And I will shew wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke:
verses.44002020: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come:
verses.44002021: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
verses.44002022: Ye men of Israel, hear these words; Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God did by him in the midst of you, as ye yourselves also know:
verses.44002023: Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain:
verses.44002024: Whom God hath raised up, having loosed the pains of death: because it was not possible that he should be holden of it.
verses.44002025: For David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved:
verses.44002036: Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.
verses.44002038: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verses.44003001: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.
verses.44003002: And a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
verses.44003003: Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms.
verses.44003004: And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us.
verses.44003005: And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.
verses.44003006: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
verses.44003007: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.
verses.44003008: And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
verses.44003009: And all the people saw him walking and praising God:
verses.44003010: And they knew that it was he which sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him.
verses.44003011: And as the lame man which was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch that is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.
verses.44003012: ¶ And when Peter saw it, he answered unto the people, Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this? or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?
verses.44004001: And as they spake unto the people, the priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees, came upon them,
verses.44004002: Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
verses.44004003: And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold unto the next day: for it was now eventide.
verses.44004004: Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand.
verses.44004005: ¶ And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes,
verses.44004006: And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.
verses.44004007: And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?
verses.44004008: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,
verses.44004009: If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole;
verses.44004010: Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him doth this man stand here before you whole.
verses.44004011: This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.
verses.44004012: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.44004013: ¶ Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
verses.44004019: But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye.
verses.44004020: For we can not but speak the things which we have seen and heard.
verses.44005001: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
verses.44005002: And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
verses.44005003: But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
verses.44005004: Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
verses.44005005: And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.
verses.44005006: And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.
verses.44005007: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.
verses.44005008: And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.
verses.44005009: Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.
verses.44005010: Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.
verses.44005011: And great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.
verses.44005015: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.
verses.44005029: ¶ Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
verses.44008014: Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
verses.44008015: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
verses.44008016: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
verses.44008017: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
verses.44008018: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,
verses.44008019: Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.
verses.44008020: But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
verses.44008021: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
verses.44008022: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
verses.44008023: For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
verses.44008024: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.
verses.44008025: And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.
verses.44009032: ¶ And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters, he came down also to the saints which dwelt at Lydda.
verses.44009033: And there he found a certain man named Æneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.
verses.44009034: And Peter said unto him, Æneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.
verses.44009035: And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord.
verses.44009036: ¶ Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
verses.44009037: And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.
verses.44009038: And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them.
verses.44009039: Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
verses.44009040: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
verses.44009041: And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive.
verses.44009042: And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.
verses.44009043: And it came to pass, that he tarried many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.
verses.44010001: There was a certain man in Cæsarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,
verses.44010002: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.
verses.44010003: He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.
verses.44010004: And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.
verses.44010005: And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:
verses.44010006: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side: he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.
verses.44010007: And when the angel which spake unto Cornelius was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;
verses.44010008: And when he had declared all these things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.
verses.44010009: ¶ On the morrow, as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour:
verses.44010010: And he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance,
verses.44010011: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
verses.44010012: Wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.
verses.44010014: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.
verses.44010024: And the morrow after they entered into Cæsarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.
verses.44010034: ¶ Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
verses.44010035: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.
verses.44011001: And the apostles and brethren that were in Judæa heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
verses.44011002: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
verses.44011003: Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.
verses.44011004: But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them, saying,
verses.44011005: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me:
verses.44011006: Upon the which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.
verses.44011007: And I heard a voice saying unto me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat.
verses.44011008: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.
verses.44011009: But the voice answered me again from heaven, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.
verses.44011010: And this was done three times: and all were drawn up again into heaven.
verses.44011011: And, behold, immediately there were three men already come unto the house where I was, sent from Cæsarea unto me.
verses.44011012: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting. Moreover these six brethren accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house:
verses.44012003: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)
verses.44012004: And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.
verses.44012005: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.
verses.44012006: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.
verses.44012007: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
verses.44012008: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And so he did. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
verses.44012009: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.
verses.44012010: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.
verses.44012011: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
verses.44012012: And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.
verses.44012013: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.
verses.44012014: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
verses.44012017: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.
verses.44015007: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
verses.44015008: And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
verses.44015009: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
verses.44015010: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
verses.44015011: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.
verses.46001012: Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.
verses.46003022: Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; all are yours;
verses.46009005: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
verses.46015005: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:
verses.48001018: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
verses.48002007: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
verses.48002009: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
verses.48002011: But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
verses.48002012: For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.
verses.48002013: And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.
verses.48002014: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
verses.60001001: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
verses.60005012: By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand.
verses.60005013: The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you; and so doth Marcus my son.
verses.61001001: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ:
verses.61001014: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.
